rules.title: Written WC eligibility notice to workplace-crime victims
rules.plain_english: If an employee is the victim of a crime at work, you must give them written notice that they are eligible for workers' compensation.

parameters.trigger: employee is victim of workplace crime
parameters.content: employee is eligible for workers' compensation

rules.applies_to: Employer-contractors subject to workers' compensation law
rules.verbatim_quote: Give any employee who is a victim of workplace crime written notification that the employee is eligible for workers’ compensation (Labor Code §3553).
rules.notes: Listed among the mandatory employee notification and posting requirements (list begins on PDF page 46).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.47. Labor Code 3553 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Tell injured employee which physician will treat them
rules.plain_english: When an employee is injured, you or your workers' comp insurer should tell the employee which physician will provide care.
rules.citation: None cited on this page (Labor Code workers' compensation provisions)
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor or their insurance company should notify an employee, in case of an injury, of a physician who will provide professional care.
rules.notes: Phrased as 'should' in the source; no specific deadline stated.

rules.title: Authorize medical treatment within 1 working day of claim form; $10,000 cap until decision
rules.plain_english: Within one working day after receiving an employee's workers' comp claim form, the employer must authorize medical treatment and keep providing it until the claim is accepted or rejected. Until that decision, medical liability is capped at $10,000. Treatment must follow ACOEM guidelines or the state treatment utilization schedule.

parameters.treatment_standard: ACOEM Occupational Medicine Practice Guidelines or Administrative Director treatment utilization schedule

rules.applies_to: Employers (including employer-contractors) receiving a workers' compensation claim form
rules.verbatim_quote: Within one working day of receiving the employee’s claim form, the employer must authorize treatment for the alleged industrial injury and must continue to provide the treatment until the date that liability for the claim is either accepted or rejected by the employer. Until the date the claim is accepted or rejected, liability for medical treatment is limited to $10,000
rules.notes: In practice the insurer usually handles authorization for insured employers.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.47. Labor Code 4600, 4604.5, 4610, 5307.27 and 5402 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 1-working-day and $10,000 values cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Supplemental job displacement benefit if no return to work within 60 days
rules.plain_english: An injured worker may get a supplemental job displacement benefit (for retraining, skill enhancement or job placement) if they cannot return to work for you within 60 days after temporary disability ends.
rules.verbatim_quote: The worker may be entitled to a supplemental job displacement benefit if they cannot return to work for the employer within 60 days following the end of the temporary disability period.
rules.notes: Benefit amount not stated in the source.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.47. Labor Code 4658.5 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Caution (not verifiable here): the book ties the benefit to the permanent disability level under LC 4658.5, which appears to describe the pre-2013 benefit; for injuries on or after 1/1/2013 the benefit is believed to be a fixed-amount voucher under LC 4658.7. Check before computing any benefit amount.

rules.title: Temporary disability: 3-day wait, two-thirds of weekly earnings, wait waived after 14 days or hospitalization
rules.plain_english: Temporary disability payments start after the third day of disability and equal two-thirds of weekly earnings up to a legal maximum. If disability lasts more than 14 days or requires overnight hospitalization, the three-day waiting period is eliminated.
rules.applies_to: Employers of injured workers / their WC insurers
rules.verbatim_quote: These weekly payments begin after the third day of disability and are based upon two-thirds of the weekly earnings, up to a legal maximum. ... Where temporary disability extends beyond 14 days or requires overnight hospitalization, the three-day waiting period is eliminated (Labor Code §§4453, 4650, 4652, and 4653).
rules.notes: Current maximum weekly rate is not given; source says the insurer can provide current rates.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.47. Labor Code 4453, 4650, 4652 and 4653 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 3-day wait, the 14-day/overnight-hospitalization exception and the two-thirds rate cannot be checked against primary text. The book gives no maximum weekly rate.

rules.title: Permanent disability and death benefits exist
rules.plain_english: A worker with a permanent disability from a job injury gets compensation based on the rated degree of disability. If the injury causes death, the deceased's dependents receive a benefit and burial expenses are allowed up to a prescribed amount.

parameters.permanent_disability_basis: rated degree of disability and worker's earnings
parameters.death_benefit_recipients: persons dependent on deceased at time of injury
parameters.burial_expenses: allowed up to a prescribed amount (amount not stated)

rules.applies_to: Employers of injured workers / their WC insurers
rules.verbatim_quote: If a permanent disability arises out of an industrial injury, the worker is entitled to compensation based on the rated degree of disability. ... If the injury causes death, a benefit is payable to those dependent on the deceased for support at the time of injury.
rules.notes: No dollar amounts given in the source.

rules.title: Serious and willful employer misconduct: compensation increased by one-half; not insurable
rules.plain_english: If an employee is hurt because of the serious or willful misconduct of the employer or its managers, the compensation is increased by one-half plus up to $250 in costs. The insurer is not liable for this increase and cannot cover it, so the contractor pays it directly.
rules.verbatim_quote: The amount of compensation otherwise recoverable can be increased one-half, together with costs and expenses not to exceed $250, where the employee is injured by reason of the serious or willful misconduct of the employer or their managing representative, partner, executive, managing officer, or general superintendent. The insurance company is not liable for the increase
rules.notes: Insurance Code 11661 bars the policy from covering this increase.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.48. Labor Code 4550/4553 and Insurance Code 11661 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Failing to secure workers' comp is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: Not carrying workers' compensation coverage (or approved self-insurance) when required is a crime (misdemeanor).

parameters.violation: failure to secure payment of compensation

rules.verbatim_quote: Failure to secure payment of compensation as required by law is a misdemeanor (Labor Code §3700.5).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.48. Labor Code 3700.5 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Only cross-referenced, in B&P 7011.4(a) on PDF p.230. Related B&P text that is in the book: B&P 7125.4(b) (PDF p.370) makes a responsible qualifier guilty of a misdemeanor for employing workers without coverage. That does not verify LC 3700.5 itself.

rules.title: No workers' comp: automatic license suspension (B&P 7125.2); discipline for willful violation (B&P 7110(c))
rules.plain_english: If you are required to carry workers' comp and you don't, or you let it lapse, your license is automatically suspended by law. The suspension starts on the lapse date, or on the date coverage was first required, and lasts until you prove coverage (B&P 7125.2). A willful or deliberate violation of the compensation insurance laws is also grounds for CSLB discipline, including revocation (B&P 7110(c)). Employing workers without coverage carries minimum civil penalties of $10,000 (sole owner) or $20,000 (partnership, corporation, LLC or tribal business) per violation (B&P 7125.4).

parameters.violation: failure to obtain or maintain workers' compensation coverage when required

automatic_suspension.effective_on: earlier of (1) date the WC coverage lapses or (2) date WC coverage was required to be obtained
automatic_suspension.reinstatement: any time, on proof of compliance per B&P 7125 and 7125.1

discretionary_discipline.mental_state: willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the compensation insurance laws

parameters.renewal_or_reinstatement_blocked_until: current and valid Certificate of WC Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the licensee's business name (B&P 7125.4(c))

rules.citation: B&P 7125.2 (automatic suspension); B&P 7110(c) (discipline for willful/deliberate violation); B&P 7125.4 (civil penalties)
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 48 (summary); PDF page 351 (B&P 7110); PDF pages 369-370 (B&P 7125.2, 7125.4)
rules.verbatim_quote: B&P 7125.2: "The failure of a licensee to obtain or maintain workers’ compensation insurance coverage, if required under this chapter, shall result in the automatic suspension of the license by operation of law ... (a) The license suspension imposed by this section is effective upon the earlier of either of the following: (1) On the date that the relevant workers’ compensation insurance coverage lapses. (2) On the date that workers’ compensation coverage is required to be obtained." | B&P 7110: "Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of ... (c) The safety laws or labor laws or compensation insurance laws or Unemployment Insurance Code of the state ... constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee."
rules.notes: Book summary (PDF p.48) reads: "A contractor’s license may be suspended or revoked by the registrar of contractors if the contractor fails to secure the payment of compensation (Business and Professions Code §7110)." Corrected against the statutory text in Ch. 8.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.48 (summary); PDF p.351 B&P 7110; PDF p.369-370 B&P 7125.2, 7125.4
verification.correction: The book summary says the registrar "may" suspend or revoke for failure to secure compensation, and cites 7110. But B&P 7110(c) makes only a "willful or deliberate disregard and violation" of the compensation insurance laws a cause for discipline. The direct license consequence is B&P 7125.2: failing to obtain or maintain required WC coverage causes AUTOMATIC suspension by operation of law. It takes effect on the earlier of the coverage-lapse date or the date coverage was first required, and is lifted only on proof of compliance (7125, 7125.1). Also added the B&P 7125.4(a) civil penalties: at least $10,000 per violation for a sole owner and at least $20,000 for an entity, with subsequent violations up to $30,000 total per occurrence (as amended by SB 291, effective 1/1/2026). Title, plain_english, parameters, citation and quote updated.

rules.title: DLSE Stop Order: no employee labor until insured
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner (DLSE) can issue a Stop Order barring an uninsured contractor from using employee labor until workers' comp insurance is in place.

parameters.issuer: DIR Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

rules.applies_to: Contractors that fail to secure workers' compensation
rules.verbatim_quote: Issuing a “Stop Order,” prohibiting the use of employee labor until insurance is provided (Labor Code §3710.1).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.48. Labor Code 3710.1 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: DLSE may get a superior court restraining order
rules.plain_english: The DLSE can go to superior court for a restraining order against a contractor that has no workers' comp coverage.

parameters.issuer: DIR Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

rules.applies_to: Contractors that fail to secure workers' compensation
rules.verbatim_quote: Obtaining a restraining order in superior court against the contractor (Labor Code §3712).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.48. Labor Code 3712 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Uninsured penalty: greater of 2x premiums or $1,000 per employee
rules.plain_english: If you are caught without workers' comp, the penalty can be the greater of twice the premiums you would have paid while uninsured or $1,000 per employee employed during that period.
rules.applies_to: Uninsured employer-contractors (status discovered without a pending claim)
rules.verbatim_quote: Penalties for an uninsured contractor may be either the greater of twice the amount the contractor would have paid in premiums during the period they were uninsured, or $1,000 per employee employed during that same period.
rules.notes: Text continues from the 'penalty assessment order' bullet on PDF page 48.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.48-49. Labor Code 3722 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 2x-premium / $1,000-per-employee formula cannot be checked against primary text. Caution (not verifiable here): current LC 3722 is believed to use $1,500 per employee, and may count employees at the time the stop order or penalty is issued rather than over the whole uninsured period. Check the current Labor Code before hard-coding $1,000.

rules.title: Uninsured penalty after a claim: $2,000 or $10,000 per employee
rules.plain_english: If your uninsured status is discovered after a workers' comp claim is filed, the penalty is $2,000 per employee employed on the date of injury if the claim is non-compensable, or $10,000 per employee if it is compensable.

parameters.trigger: uninsured status discovered after filing of a claim for compensation
parameters.employee_count_basis: employees employed on the date of injury

rules.applies_to: Uninsured employer-contractors with a filed WC claim
rules.verbatim_quote: If the contractor’s uninsured status is discovered following the filing of a claim for compensation, the penalty shall be either $2,000 for each employee employed on the date of injury in non-compensable cases, or $10,000 for each employee in compensable cases (Labor Code §3722).)

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.49. Labor Code 3722 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The $2,000 / $10,000 per-employee amounts cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: DLSE lien on uninsured contractor's real and personal property
rules.plain_english: The state can record a lien against an uninsured contractor's real and personal property as security for amounts owed.

parameters.issuer: DIR Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

rules.applies_to: Contractors that fail to secure workers' compensation
rules.verbatim_quote: Recording a lien against the real property and personal property of the contractor as a security interest (Labor Code §3727).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.49. Labor Code 3727 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Willfully uninsured + injury: compensation + 10% penalty + attorney fees + civil liability
rules.plain_english: If you willfully go without workers' comp and an employee is injured, you must pay the disability compensation plus a 10% penalty and attorney fees, provide all needed medical treatment, and you can be sued for damages with negligence presumed. The employee's own negligence is not a defense.
rules.applies_to: Contractors who willfully fail to provide compensation insurance
rules.verbatim_quote: If a contractor willfully fails to provide compensation insurance for an employee and an injury occurs, the contractor must pay the disability compensation plus a penalty of 10 percent and attorney fees. They must also supply all necessary medical treatment. In addition, they are liable for damages in a civil action, with a legal presumption that the injury was caused by the employer’s negligence.
rules.notes: Source continues: 'Contributory negligence of the employee is no defense'.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.49. Labor Code 3706, 3708, 4554 and 4555 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 10% penalty cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Willful safety violation causing death or prolonged impairment: fine and/or imprisonment
rules.plain_english: An employer, or a supervisor who directs other employees, who willfully violates a safety or health standard that causes an employee's death or prolonged bodily impairment can be fined and/or imprisoned on conviction.

result: prolonged impairment of body of employee
liable_persons: employee having direction, management control, or custody of employment of other employees

rules.verbatim_quote: Every employer, and every employee having direction, management control, or custody of employment of any other employee, who willfully violates any occupational safety or health standard that causes the death of any employee or the prolonged impairment of the body of any employee shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine and or imprisonment (Labor Code §6425).
rules.notes: Fine and prison amounts not stated in the source.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.49. Labor Code 6425 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The book states no fine or prison amounts.

rules.title: Keep records required by B&P 7111 and for audits/tax
rules.plain_english: Keep the business records that Contractors State License Law requires (B&P 7111) and that government agencies need for audits and tax reporting.
rules.verbatim_quote: State and federal agencies frequently specify that certain records must be maintained and made available for government audits and to substantiate tax reporting. For a description of the records specifically required under Contractors State License Law, see Business and Professions Code section 7111.
rules.notes: The record types and retention period in B&P 7111 are not stated on this page; pull them from the Law Sections chunk.

rules.title: Accrual accounting required for federal tax when inventories used; cash basis not recommended
rules.plain_english: If your business uses inventories, federal tax rules require the accrual method. CSLB does not recommend cash-basis accounting for contractors because it does not match job income with job costs.

parameters.accrual_definition: revenue recognized when earned, expenses when incurred

rules.citation: None cited (federal income tax rule described in CSLB guidance)
rules.verbatim_quote: For federal income tax purposes, the accrual method is required when inventories are utilized. ... For these reasons, the cash basis of accounting is not recommended for contractors.
rules.notes: Federal tax rules have small-business exceptions that this book does not mention; check with a CPA.

rules.title: Percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
rules.plain_english: Under the percentage-of-completion method, you recognize revenue and profit in proportion to the work completed. For example, 50% of the work done means 50% of estimated revenue and profit is earned.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with qualifying long-term projects using accrual accounting
rules.verbatim_quote: The percentage of completion method will report profits and losses regularly based on work accomplished on each job. For example, if the work performed each year is estimated to represent 50 percent of total performance under contract, then 50 percent of the total estimated revenue and profit is considered earned.
rules.notes: Accounting method, not a licensing requirement.

rules.title: Completed-contract revenue recognition
rules.plain_english: Under the completed-contract method, all gross income and related costs of a contract are reported in the year the contract is completed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with qualifying long-term projects using accrual accounting
rules.verbatim_quote: The completed contract method allows for the gross income and related costs for each contract to be reported in the year in which such a contract is completed.
rules.notes: Federal tax eligibility limits for this method are not stated here.

rules.title: Retention: usually 10% withheld from progress payments
rules.plain_english: Retention is an amount, usually 10%, held back from each progress payment until the project is satisfactorily completed and accepted. It is earned money, carried as a current asset.

parameters.released_upon: satisfactory completion and final acceptance of the project

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors receiving progress payments; owners withholding retention
rules.verbatim_quote: Retention: A specified amount, usually 10 percent, withheld from progress payments to the contractor pending satisfactory completion and final acceptance of the project. You have already earned this amount even though you have not yet been paid.
rules.notes: 'Usually 10 percent' describes common practice, not a legal cap. These pages do not cover California's statutory retention limits and release deadlines (for example the public works retention caps in the Public Contract Code and the private works retention release rules in the Civil Code), so check those separately before setting a default.

rules.title: Current vs. long-term: one-year line
rules.plain_english: On the balance sheet, current assets are cash or items convertible to cash within one year. Current liabilities are debts due within one year. Long-term liabilities are due more than one year after the balance sheet date.
rules.verbatim_quote: These are the assets that are either cash or capable of being converted into cash in the normal course of business, generally within one year from the date of the balance sheet. ... Current Liabilities: This item includes debts of the company that are due within one year of the balance sheet date. ... Long-term liabilities are notes or mortgages due one year beyond the balance sheet date.
rules.notes: Each part of the quote comes from a different page (54, 55 and 56).

rules.title: Fixed assets valued at original cost less accumulated depreciation
rules.plain_english: Equipment, tools and other fixed assets are carried at their original cost minus accumulated depreciation, not at market value.
rules.verbatim_quote: Regardless of their current market value, fixed assets are valued at their original cost less accumulated depreciation.
rules.notes: Leased property is often shown with fixed assets, and lease payments with liabilities.

rules.title: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities
rules.plain_english: Working capital is total current assets minus total current liabilities.
rules.verbatim_quote: The difference between the total current assets and the total current liabilities is called working capital.
rules.notes: This page gives no statutory minimum. The CSLB working-capital requirement for license applicants, if any, appears elsewhere in the law.

rules.title: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities
rules.plain_english: The current ratio is total current assets divided by total current liabilities. In the book's example, $250,000 / $180,000 = 1.39.
rules.verbatim_quote: To calculate the current ratio, divide total current assets by total current liabilities.
rules.notes: No target ratio is mandated.

rules.title: Quick ratio = (current assets - inventories) / current liabilities
rules.plain_english: The quick ratio uses quick assets (current assets minus inventories) divided by current liabilities. In the book's example, $140,000 / $180,000 = 0.78.
rules.verbatim_quote: One simple method of determining the quick assets is total current assets minus inventories.

rules.title: Debt-to-net-worth and efficiency ratios
rules.plain_english: Lenders look at total liabilities divided by net worth. Efficiency is measured by net sales to net working capital, net sales to total assets, and net income to net worth.
rules.verbatim_quote: The long-term creditors (banks or insurance companies) would be interested in the ratio of total liabilities to net worth. ... Net sales to net working capital, net sales to total assets, and net income to net worth are all measures of the efficiency of the company’s use of its resources.

rules.title: Typical payment structure: 3+ payments, 90% during construction, 10% retention
rules.plain_english: A typical custom-building or remodeling contract has three or more payments. 90% is paid during construction and the final 10% (retention) after completion and expiration of the lien period.

parameters.final_payment_trigger: completion and expiration of the lien period

rules.applies_to: Custom building and remodeling contracts (typical practice)
rules.verbatim_quote: The typical contract provides for three or more payments, 90 percent during the construction phase and the final 10 percent upon completion and expiration of the lien period. This final 10 percent is the “retention.”
rules.notes: Describes typical practice, not a statutory schedule. Home improvement contracts carry their own statutory down payment and progress payment limits (B&P 7159), which are not restated here.

rules.title: Cannot collect more than the percentage of work completed
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not bill or collect more than the percentage of the work already completed.
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CSLB business guidance); related home improvement progress-payment rule in B&P 7159 (not cited here)
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor cannot ... collect more than the percentage already completed.
rules.notes: Stated generally in the business management chapter. For home improvement contracts the statutory rule is in B&P 7159; cross-check that chunk.

rules.title: Retention released only after whole project accepted
rules.plain_english: Retention is released only after the entire project is accepted, even if your own work finished early. Subcontractors who finish early may wait a long time, so plan cash flow (possibly borrowing).

parameters.risk: early-finishing subcontractors wait for project acceptance

rules.verbatim_quote: Retention payments to the individual contractor may be held up through no fault of the contractor. The total project must be ... accepted before retentions are released.
rules.notes: These pages give no statutory deadlines for releasing retention after completion. California prompt payment and retention statutes are outside this chunk.

rules.title: Estimate must include sales tax, freight, burdened labor, direct and indirect costs
rules.plain_english: Bid estimates should include sales tax and freight on materials. Do not deduct cash discounts unless you are sure you can pay within the discount period. Labor must include payroll taxes, benefits, vacation and insurance, along with permits, financing costs, equipment and indirect costs.

parameters.exclude_cash_discounts_unless: funds certain to pay within discount period

rules.verbatim_quote: It is important to include sales tax and freight costs. Cash discounts should not be included unless the contractor is certain that sufficient financial resources will be available so that accounts payable may be repaid during the discount period.
rules.notes: Best-practice guidance; useful as an estimating checklist.

rules.title: Add overhead and profit to every bid
rules.plain_english: After totaling job costs, add overhead (office rent, supplies, office wages, advertising, bad debts, storage, other admin costs) and then add profit. Omitting profit seriously jeopardizes the business.
rules.verbatim_quote: The contractor also must identify the overhead expenses. Overhead normally includes such expenses as office rental, supplies and wages, advertising, bad debts, storage charges, and any other general administrative costs. When all the costs have been totaled, the contractor must add profit.
rules.notes: The pitfalls on page 65 (bidding without understanding the plans, overextension, bidding against competitors instead of the job) are also useful bid-review checks.

rules.title: Schedule with bar chart or critical path method
rules.plain_english: The estimate becomes the project budget and a schedule. A bar chart shows task start and finish dates. The critical path method links dependent tasks, and any delay on a critical-path task delays the whole project.

parameters.cpm_rule: delay on any critical-path task = delay of project completion

rules.verbatim_quote: The critical path method (Figure 6.B) is a more complex tool that better interrelates the tasks. ... Any delay in one of these tasks will result in an overall delay of the project.
rules.notes: Figures 6.A and 6.B (pages 66-67) are images with no extractable text.

rules.title: Design an insurance package; review coverage yearly
rules.plain_english: Work with an agent or broker on an insurance package that can include workers' comp, fire, liability, auto, fidelity bonds, business interruption, employee health and life, and key-person coverage. Cover the largest exposure first, use deductibles to cut cost, and review property and liability coverage every year.
rules.verbatim_quote: Insurance is a means of reducing the company’s exposure to risk. The contractor should consult an insurance agent or broker to design a comprehensive insurance package to meet the company’s specific needs. ... Reviewing coverage yearly to reflect changes in the business.
rules.notes: Of these coverages, only workers' comp (if you have employees) is legally mandatory per other sections. The rest is guidance.

rules.title: Four owner-builder contract types
rules.plain_english: Common owner-builder contract types are lump-sum, cost-plus, unit-price and guaranteed-maximum cost. Standard forms are available from trade associations, AIA and AGC, and an attorney should check contracts for regulatory compliance.

parameters.recommended_review: attorney check for compliance with regulatory agency requirements

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners entering construction contracts
rules.verbatim_quote: There are typically four types of contractual agreements between the builder and owner with which the contractor should be familiar. These are the lump-sum, the cost-plus, the unit-price, and the guaranteed-maximum cost contract.

rules.title: Put significant contracts in writing
rules.plain_english: Some contracts are legally required to be in writing, and any contract of significance should be written so the parties' rights and intent are clear if a dispute arises.

parameters.applies_when: statutorily required, and recommended for any contract of significance

rules.citation: None cited on this page (statutory writing requirements, e.g., home improvement contracts, appear elsewhere)
rules.verbatim_quote: Besides the statutory requirement that certain contracts be in writing, it is extremely important that a contract of any ... significance at all be in writing.
rules.notes: Which contracts are statutorily required to be written is not specified on this page.

rules.title: Document changes and get a signed written change order
rules.plain_english: When the customer requests something different from the contract (more or less work), document it in writing, negotiate the cost and time impact right away, let the customer decide, and have both parties sign a written change order.

parameters.trigger: request differs from original agreement (more or less)
steps: immediately negotiate cost and time effect
inform customer and let customer decide
both parties sign written change order

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on any project with changes/extras
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CSLB guidance; home improvement extra-work rules appear in B&P 7159 elsewhere)
rules.verbatim_quote: Once you determine that a request is different than what was agreed to (whether more or less), document that fact in writing. You should also immediately negotiate the effect of the change, such as cost and time. ... If you and your customer agree to the change, make sure both parties sign the written change order.
rules.notes: Statutory content requirements for change orders on home improvement contracts are in another chunk.

rules.title: Punch lists, end-of-job walk-through, regular invoicing
rules.plain_english: Use frequent punch lists, do a walk-through near the end of the job to list remaining items, fix deficiencies quickly, document progress, and invoice regularly to keep cash flowing and the customer informed.
rules.verbatim_quote: Frequent “punch lists” are a good idea. A walk-through near the end of the job to determine the items that are left to be completed is recommended. Correct any deficiencies quickly. ... By invoicing regularly, you will minimize your business’s cash demands while keeping your customer informed.
rules.notes: Best-practice guidance.

rules.title: Small claims monetary limit $12,500
rules.plain_english: You can sue for money owed in small claims court for up to $12,500. Cases are usually heard within one to two months at minimal cost.
rules.verbatim_quote: Although you cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien in small claims court, you may get a monetary judgment of up to $12,500 (see CCP §116.221).
rules.notes: CCP 116.221 sets the limit for natural persons. A lower limit for entity plaintiffs (CCP 116.220) is not stated in this source; verify before applying $12,500 to a corporation or LLC.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.71. CCP 116.221 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. B&P text on PDF p.306 only points to CCP 116.220 "in Appendix", and the 2026 edition has no appendix. The $12,500 limit cannot be checked against primary text. The extractor's caution stands: CCP 116.220 sets a lower limit for plaintiffs that are not natural persons (believed to be $6,250), so do not apply $12,500 to a corporation or LLC without checking.

rules.title: Mechanics lien cannot be foreclosed in small claims court
rules.plain_english: Small claims court can award money but cannot foreclose a mechanics lien; lien foreclosure must be filed in superior court.
rules.verbatim_quote: Although you cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien in small claims court, you may get a monetary judgment of up to $12,500 (see CCP §116.221).
rules.notes: Lien foreclosure deadlines are in the mechanics lien rules below. The 'superior court' venue is implied, not stated.

rules.title: No attorneys in small claims
rules.plain_english: In small claims court both you and your customer must represent yourselves. Neither side may be represented by an attorney.
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CCP small claims provisions)
rules.verbatim_quote: You and your customer must represent yourselves. Neither you nor your customer may be represented by an attorney.
rules.notes: Small-claims self-help: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/small-claims-california

rules.title: Losing small claims defendant may appeal within 30 days
rules.plain_english: If the defendant loses in small claims court, they have an automatic right to appeal within 30 days of the ruling. Small claims judgments are otherwise as binding as other court judgments.
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CCP small claims provisions)
rules.verbatim_quote: If the defendant loses in small claims court, there is an automatic right of appeal within 30 days of the ruling.
rules.notes: Calendar days assumed. The source does not say whether the 30 days run from the ruling date or from mailing of notice.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.71. The CCP small-claims appeal provisions (CCP 116.710-116.795) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Caution (not verifiable here): CCP 116.750 is believed to run the 30 days from the clerk's mailing or delivery of notice of entry of judgment, not from the ruling date. The plaintiff also has no appeal on its own claim. Do not compute the deadline from the hearing date without checking.

rules.title: Residential (1-4 unit) arbitration clause: B&P 7191 title, type size and exact notice; bars CSLB arbitration
rules.plain_english: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units has an arbitration clause, the clause must be titled 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES' and set in the required bold type (or in capitals if typed). The exact B&P 7191 notice and assent statement must come right after it, before the parties' initials. A clause that does not comply may not be enforceable against anyone but the contractor. If the parties agreed to private arbitration, the dispute cannot go to CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(a)(6)).

parameters.applies_to_contracts: contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units that contain a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals
parameters.format_if_printed: at least 10-point roman boldface type, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type
parameters.notice_placement: immediately following the arbitration provision and immediately before the line or space for the parties to indicate assent or nonassent (initials)
parameters.required_notice_text: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION. IF YOU REFUSE TO SUBMIT TO ARBITRATION AFTER AGREEING TO THIS PROVISION, YOU MAY BE COMPELLED TO ARBITRATE UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS CODE OR OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS. YOUR AGREEMENT TO THIS ARBITRATION PROVISION IS VOLUNTARY.
parameters.required_assent_statement: WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THE FOREGOING AND AGREE TO SUBMIT DISPUTES ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION TO NEUTRAL ARBITRATION.
parameters.notice_format_if_printed: at least 10-point roman boldface type, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type
parameters.consequence_of_noncompliance: provision may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee (B&P 7191(c))
parameters.effect_on_cslb_arbitration: not eligible for CSLB arbitration if the parties previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise (B&P 7085(a)(6); also a criterion for mandatory referral under 7085(b))
parameters.later_waiver_exception: stated only in CSLB narrative (PDF p.72); not in B&P 7085

rules.applies_to: Contractors using arbitration clauses in contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units
rules.citation: B&P 7191 (clause title, type size, notice); B&P 7085(a)(6) (no CSLB arbitration after private arbitration agreement)
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 439-440 (B&P 7191); PDF page 324 (B&P 7085)
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled “ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES.” ... (c) A provision for arbitration of a dispute between a principal in a contract for work on a residential property with four or fewer units that does not comply with this section may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee.
rules.notes: Exact notice and assent text are in parameters.required_notice_text and required_assent_statement, checked character for character against PDF p.439. Original book summary (PDF p.72): "If you want potential disputes to be solved via private arbitration you must use the arbitration notice in Business and Professions Code section 7191 ... (unless both parties later sign a waiver of the contractual arbitration clause)."

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.72 (summary); PDF p.439-440 B&P 7191; PDF p.324 B&P 7085(a)(6)
verification.correction: The book summary says contractors "must use" the 7191 notice for any private arbitration clause. B&P 7191 actually covers only contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units. For those, the provision must be titled "ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES" and set in at least 10-pt roman boldface (or contrasting red, at least 8-pt roman boldface) if printed, or in capitals if typed. The statutory NOTICE and assent statement must follow it immediately, before the initials line. A provision that does not comply may not be enforceable against anyone other than the licensee (7191(c)). Added the exact statutory notice and assent text. The bar on CSLB arbitration comes from B&P 7085(a)(6) ("The parties have not previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise"). The "unless both parties later sign a waiver" exception appears only in the CSLB narrative (PDF p.72); B&P 7085 does not support it.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration: mandatory at or below $25,000 (bond amount); voluntary above $25,000 and under $50,000
rules.plain_english: CSLB must refer a qualifying complaint to arbitration when the contract price or the damages demanded is $25,000 or less, which is the amount of the contractor's bond. When damages are above $25,000 and below $50,000, CSLB may refer it to arbitration only if both the contractor and the complainant agree.

parameters.qualifying_complaints: verified complaint alleging violation of B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120, or any complaint arising from a contract involving works of improvement, where the registrar finds a possible violation
parameters.formula: tier = 'mandatory' if (contract_price <= 25000 or damages_demanded <= 25000) else ('voluntary' if 25000 < damages < 50000 and both_parties_agree else 'not_eligible')
parameters.cost: free (CSLB narrative, PDF p.72; not stated in statute)

rules.applies_to: Contractors subject to CSLB complaints; homeowners filing complaints
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 324-325 (B&P 7085); PDF page 295 (B&P 7071.6)
rules.verbatim_quote: For the purposes of paragraph (1), “material damages” means damages greater than the amount of the bond required under subdivision (a) of Section 7071.6, but less than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000). (b) In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration, utilizing the criteria set forth in paragraphs (2) to (6), inclusive, of subdivision (a).
rules.notes: B&P 7071.6(a) (operative 1/1/2023) sets the bond at $25,000. If the bond amount changes, both tier boundaries move with it. Original book summary (PDF p.72): "a mandatory program for disputes involving alleged damages of less than $25,000, and a voluntary program for disputes involving alleged damages of between $25,000 and $50,000."

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.72 (summary); PDF p.324-325 B&P 7085(a)-(b); PDF p.295 B&P 7071.6(a)
verification.correction: The statute sets the tier boundaries by reference to the contractor's bond, and the book gets the edges wrong. Mandatory referral (B&P 7085(b)) applies when the contract price OR the demand for damages is "equal to or less than" the B&P 7071.6 bond amount, which is $25,000 (PDF p.295). The complaint "shall be referred" with no party consent needed. So exactly $25,000 is mandatory, not voluntary, and a contract price at or under $25,000 also qualifies. Voluntary referral (7085(a)) needs the consent of both licensee and complainant and "material damages" above the bond amount but "less than" $50,000, so exactly $50,000 is out. Both tiers need a possible violation of B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120, or a complaint arising from a contract for a work of improvement. "Free" comes from the CSLB narrative only. The 7085(b) text as printed reads garbled ("but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred"); the thresholds above follow its operative words.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration eligibility criteria (B&P 7085)
rules.plain_english: CSLB can send a dispute to its arbitration program only if all of these hold: the contractor's license was in good standing at the time of the alleged violation; the contractor has no history of repeated or similar violations and no outstanding disciplinary actions; the parties have not already agreed to private arbitration; and the registrar finds arbitration serves the public better than discipline. Voluntary cases also need evidence of material damages, and the parties must be told about Civil Code 2855.
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 324-325 (B&P 7085)
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) There are reasonable grounds for the registrar to believe that the public interest would be better served by arbitration than by disciplinary action. (3) The licensee does not have a history of repeated or similar violations. (4) The licensee was in good standing at the time of the alleged violation. (5) The licensee does not have any outstanding disciplinary actions filed against him or her. (6) The parties have not previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise.
rules.notes: The book summary (PDF p.72) adds "(current and not under suspension)" to explain good standing. Original summary criterion: "The contractor cannot have a record of prior violations."

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.72 (summary); PDF p.324-325 B&P 7085(a)(1)-(7), (b)
verification.correction: The book lists three criteria. B&P 7085(a) has seven, worded differently. "Cannot have a record of prior violations" overstates the statute, which only requires that the licensee "does not have a history of repeated or similar violations" ((a)(3)). Added the missing criteria: no outstanding disciplinary actions filed against the licensee ((a)(5)); a registrar finding that the public interest is better served by arbitration than by discipline ((a)(2)); and, for voluntary referrals, evidence of material damages ((a)(1)) and that the parties were advised of Civil Code 2855 ((a)(7)). Mandatory referrals (7085(b)) use criteria (a)(2)-(6).

rules.title: Lien remedies: preliminary notice, record lien, stop notice, foreclose
rules.plain_english: Anyone who improves property may have lien rights on the property and possibly on construction funds. Perfecting them is technical and deadlines are short: serve the preliminary notice, record the mechanics lien, file a stop notice, and sue to foreclose.
rules.citation: None cited on this page (Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law)
rules.verbatim_quote: You should be thoroughly familiar with the manner and means of perfecting your lien rights, such as giving the preliminary notice, recording the mechanics lien, filing a stop notice, and filing suit to foreclose. These remedies can be utilized by anyone who improves the property.
rules.notes: The CSLB guide uses pre-2012 terminology. Under the current Civil Code (8000 et seq.) a 'stop notice' is a 'stop payment notice' and an 'original contractor' is a 'direct contractor'.

rules.title: Corporations/LLCs need an attorney outside small claims
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC cannot represent itself in court except in small claims and must hire an attorney. Sole proprietors and partners may represent themselves.
rules.verbatim_quote: If you are a corporation or limited liability company, you cannot represent yourself in court other than small claims court and must obtain the services of an attorney. If you are a partner or a sole proprietor, you can represent yourself in court and are not required to have an attorney represent you.

rules.title: Breach-of-contract suit available even without lien rights
rules.plain_english: Even if you missed the mechanics lien deadlines, you can still sue for breach of contract or on any other legal theory to collect money owed.
rules.verbatim_quote: Regardless of your mechanics lien rights, as with any other businessperson, you can file suit for breach of the construction contract if someone does not fulfill their obligation.
rules.notes: Page 74 repeats the point: 'even if you have not availed yourself of the mechanics lien rights, you still have alternative legal remedies.' Limitations periods for contract suits are not stated.

rules.title: Mechanics lien right is constitutional
rules.plain_english: The California Constitution gives mechanics, material suppliers, artisans and laborers a lien on the property they improved, for the value of their labor and materials. Statutes set how the lien is perfected.

parameters.lien_measure: value of labor done and material furnished

rules.applies_to: Contractors, subcontractors, laborers, material suppliers; property owners
rules.verbatim_quote: Mechanics, persons furnishing materials, artisans, and laborers of every class, shall have a lien upon the property upon which they have bestowed labor or furnished material for the value of such labor done and material furnished
rules.notes: The source writes the citation as 'Article 14, Section 3'.

rules.title: Lien claimant needs a contract with owner or owner's agent
rules.plain_english: You don't need a contract directly with the owner to claim a lien, but you must have one with the owner or someone treated as the owner's agent (a contractor, subcontractor, architect, builder or other person in charge of the work).

contract_required_with: other person having charge of the work of improvement

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.verbatim_quote: To file on mechanics liens does not mean that they must have a contract directly with the owner. However, they must have a contract with the agent of the owner and every contractor, subcontractor, architect, builder, or other person having charge of a work of improvement and held to be an agent of the owner.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.73. The Civil Code mechanics lien law (Civ. Code 8000 et seq.) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: A material supplier's supplier has no lien
rules.plain_english: A material supplier is not the owner's agent, so a company that sells to a material supplier (not to a contractor) has no mechanics lien right.

parameters.reason: material supplier is not agent of owner

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.verbatim_quote: A material supplier is not the agent of the owner and, therefore, a material supplier’s supplier is not entitled to a statutory lien.
rules.notes: Useful as an eligibility check: tier = supplier-to-supplier means no lien.

rules.title: Work/materials must be incorporated (installed) to perfect a lien
rules.plain_english: To perfect a mechanics lien, your work or materials must be incorporated into (installed in) the structure.
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.verbatim_quote: Further, to perfect your lien, the work and/or materials, etc. must be incorporated into the structure. That is to say, it has to be installed.
rules.notes: This is a simplified statement; the Civil Code has nuances for materials furnished but not used. Verify before using it to deny a lien.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.73. The Civil Code mechanics lien law is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The extractor's caution about materials that were furnished but not installed stands.

rules.title: No mechanics lien on public works; use stop notice
rules.plain_english: A mechanics lien is a lien on property and a stop notice is a lien on construction funds; you may use either or both. On public works you cannot record a mechanics lien, so a stop notice may be your only remedy.
rules.applies_to: Contractors, subcontractors and suppliers on public and private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.verbatim_quote: A mechanics lien is a lien on property. A stop notice is a lien on funds. You may use one or the other, or both. However, it should be noted that in public works, you cannot file a mechanics lien; therefore, your only remedy may be a stop notice.
rules.notes: Current statutes call this a 'stop payment notice'. Public works payment bond claims are another remedy that this page does not cover.

rules.title: Gather property and party information before serving notices
rules.plain_english: Before serving lien notices, get the property's legal description and the owner's name and interest. Confirm who ordered the work and whether others (such as lenders) hold an interest, determine your role (prime, sub, laborer, supplier), identify the construction lender, and consider any bond or joint control.

checklist: owner name and extent of owner's interest
whether owner requested the improvement; interests of requester and others (e.g., lenders)
your role: prime contractor, subcontractor, laborer, or material supplier
effect of a bond or joint control

rules.applies_to: All potential lien and stop notice claimants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB Mechanics Lien and Stop Notice Checklist, Part I)
rules.verbatim_quote: Obtain the legal description of the property. ... Determine the name of the construction lender (if any). ... Consider the effect of a bond or joint control.
rules.notes: Good template for a job-intake form.

rules.title: Serve Preliminary 20-day Notice within 20 days of first furnishing
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors and material suppliers must serve a Preliminary 20-day Notice on the owner, the original (prime) contractor and the construction lender within 20 days after first furnishing labor or materials. Only one notice is needed per job, however many deliveries you make.

parameters.trigger: first furnishing of labor or materials

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code preliminary notice provisions (Civ. Code 8200-8216)
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 20 days from first furnishing labor or materials, serve a “Preliminary 20-day Notice” on the owner, the original contractor, and construction lender. No matter how many deliveries you make, or the time span over which you furnish labor or materials, only one Preliminary Notice is required.
rules.notes: The Civil Code range is the extractor's cross-reference, not printed in the source. Two points also come from the extractor, not this source, and should be verified: under current law a late notice generally covers only work furnished within 20 days before service and after, and some direct contractors must also give notice to the construction lender.

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.75; PDF p.402-403 B&P 7159(e)(4)
verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75. Civil Code 8200-8216 are not reproduced in the law book. Partial support from B&P text in the book: the statutory Mechanics Lien Warning in B&P 7159(e)(4) (PDF p.402-403) says "The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material." It also says owners do not get preliminary notices from the prime contractor or laborers. That supports the 20-day figure. The service list (owner, original contractor, lender) and the effect of late service remain unchecked.

rules.title: Preliminary notice must include owner-responsibility wording
rules.plain_english: The preliminary notice must include specific statutory wording that tells the owner of their responsibility to notify everyone who served a preliminary notice (for example, when a Notice of Completion or Cessation is recorded).

parameters.required_content: statement informing owner of duty to notify those who served a Preliminary Notice

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers serving preliminary notices
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code preliminary notice content provisions
rules.verbatim_quote: The notice must include specific wording to inform a property owner of a new responsibility to notify anyone else who served a Preliminary Notice.
rules.notes: The exact statutory wording is not reproduced in this source; take it from the Civil Code (preliminary notice form) before generating a notice.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75. The required statutory wording does not appear anywhere in the law book; the Civil Code preliminary-notice form is not included. The exact text must come from the Civil Code.

rules.title: Optional: file preliminary notice with county recorder to be alerted of NOC/NOCessation
rules.plain_english: You may also file your preliminary notice with the county recorder where the property is located. The recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, which shortens your lien deadline.

parameters.file_with: county recorder of county where property is located
parameters.benefit: recorder notifies you when Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded

rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: You may also file the Preliminary 20-day Notice with the county recorder in the county in which the property is located. The county recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded on the property.

rules.title: How to serve the preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: Serve the preliminary notice by first-class certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. Address it to the recipient's residence or business, the address on the building permit, or the address on a recorded mortgage or trust deed. Personal delivery, or leaving it with an adult in charge at the residence or business, also works. Keep the post office receipts as proof.

mail_methods: first class certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid
first class registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid
valid_addresses: residence or place of business of person served
address on recorded mortgage or trust deed
alternative_methods: leaving with adult person in charge at residence or place of business

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice service provisions
rules.verbatim_quote: The most common method for serving a notice is to use first class certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed to the residence or place of business of the person being served, or at the address shown by the building permit, or at an address contained on a recorded mortgage or trust deed.

rules.title: Stop work under the contract once a Notice of Completion is recorded
rules.plain_english: Once a Notice of Completion has been recorded (it requires the owner's or owner's agent's signature), do no additional work under that contract.

parameters.action: do not perform additional work under the contract

rules.verbatim_quote: If the owner records a Notice of Completion after completion of work of improvement (this requires signature of owner or owner’s agent), you should not do additional work under the contract.
rules.notes: Repeated for prime contractors on pages 76-77 ('Do not do additional work under the contract').

rules.title: Owner may record Notice of Cessation only after 30 days of no labor
rules.plain_english: An owner may record a Notice of Cessation only after labor on the job has stopped for at least 30 days.
rules.applies_to: Project owners; lien claimants tracking deadlines
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice of cessation provision
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 75 and 77
rules.verbatim_quote: Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation.
rules.notes: Current law refers to a continuous 30-day cessation (extractor's note; verify).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.75 and p.77
verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75 and p.77. The Civil Code notice-of-cessation provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Subcontractor: record lien within 30 days after owner records NOC or Notice of Cessation
rules.plain_english: If the owner records a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation, a subcontractor or supplier must record its Claim of Lien with the county recorder within 30 days of that recording, and serve stop notices at the same time.

parameters.trigger: owner records Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines for claimants other than direct contractors
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 30 days of the owner recording either a Notice of Cessation or Completion, the subcontractor must ... record a Claim of Lien with the county recorder. Also at this time, serve stop notices (see below).
rules.notes: Confirmed by the glossary on page 79 (30 days for a subcontractor if the NOC is recorded). The book frames the trigger as the date of recording.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75-76. The Civil Code lien-recording deadline for claimants other than direct contractors is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. It is consistent with the glossary on PDF p.79 (30 days for a subcontractor after an NOC).

rules.title: Owner must notify potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording NOC/NOCessation
rules.plain_english: An owner who records a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation must notify potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording, so they know their lien deadline was shortened. This does not apply to residential property with four or fewer units.

parameters.trigger: owner records Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation
parameters.notify: potential lien claimants (those who gave preliminary notice)
parameters.exempt_if: residential property of four or fewer units

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code owner notice provision
rules.verbatim_quote: An owner who files a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion must notify any potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording the notices. This notification is designed to let you, the potential lien claimant, know that the time for filing a Claim of Lien has been reduced. This provision does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units.
rules.notes: The consequence of an owner's failure to notify is not stated here. Under the Civil Code, the shortened deadline may not apply to a claimant who was not notified (extractor's note; verify).

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76. The Civil Code owner-notice provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 10-day duty and the exemption for residential property of four or fewer units cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: File lien foreclosure within 90 days of recording the lien; record lis pendens
rules.plain_english: Within 90 days after recording your Claim of Lien, file a lawsuit to foreclose it and record a lis pendens at the same time. If you served a stop notice, file suit on it then too. Otherwise the lien is lost.

concurrent_actions: file action on stop notice (if applicable)

rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants (prime contractors, subcontractors, suppliers)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien foreclosure deadline
rules.verbatim_quote: File Lien Foreclosure Action within 90 days of recording a Claim of Lien and record a lis pendens at the same time. You must also file an action on the stop notice at this time, if applicable.
rules.notes: Repeated for prime contractors on page 77. The source does not mention how an unenforced lien is released, or the statutory timing window for suit on a stop payment notice; verify the latter against the current Civil Code.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76-77. The Civil Code lien-foreclosure deadline is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The phrase "Otherwise the lien is lost" in plain_english is the extractor's inference. The book does not state the consequence.

rules.title: No NOC/NOCessation recorded: record lien within 90 days of use+cessation or acceptance
rules.plain_english: If no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, prime contractors, subcontractors and suppliers must record their Claim of Lien within 90 days after labor ceases and the owner uses the work, or after the owner accepts the work. Subs and suppliers should serve stop notices at the same time.

triggers: labor ceases and owner/agent uses the work of improvement
parameters.precondition: no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation recorded

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors, subcontractors and material suppliers on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines
rules.verbatim_quote: If no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded and either: (a) Labor ceases and the owner or agent uses work of improvement, or (b) The owner or agent accepts improvement, then: (1) Within 90 days of any of the above acts, record a Claim of Lien. Also, at this time, serve stop notices (see below).

rules.title: Who to serve stop notices on; surety if payment bond recorded
rules.plain_english: Serve stop notices on the owner, bonded stop notices on the construction lender, or on anyone else holding construction funds. If no mechanics lien has been recorded and a surety payment bond has been recorded, serve the surety. File suit on the notice when you file the lien foreclosure.

parameters.surety_service_required_if: no mechanics lien recorded AND surety payment bond recorded
parameters.suit_timing: same time as lien foreclosure action

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice and payment bond provisions
rules.verbatim_quote: Serve stop notices on the owner, bonded stop notices on the construction lender, or anyone holding funds. (b) If no mechanics lien has been recorded, and a surety payment bond has been recorded, then the notice must be served on the surety. rules.title: Prime contractor: Notice of Completion within 15 days after completion (owner signature)
rules.plain_english: Within 15 days after completion, a Notice of Completion may be recorded. It must be signed by the owner or owner's agent. After that, do no more work under the contract.
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision

rules.title: Prime contractor: record lien within 60 days after NOC or Notice of Cessation
rules.plain_english: If a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, the prime (original) contractor must record its Claim of Lien within 60 days of that recording, then foreclose within 90 days of recording the lien.

parameters.trigger: recording of Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation

rules.title: 'Claim of lien' and 'mechanics lien' mean the same (AB 457)
rules.plain_english: Since AB 457 (effective 2011), 'claim of lien' and 'mechanics lien' have the same legal definition.
rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: Per AB 457, which took effect in 2011, the definitions of “claim of lien” and “mechanics lien” are the same.

rules.title: Serve Notice of Mechanics Lien with signed proof of service affidavit or lien is unenforceable
rules.plain_english: When you record a mechanics lien, serve a Notice of Mechanics Lien on the owner (or reputed owner), or on the construction lender or original contractor. The person who served it must complete and sign a proof of service affidavit. Without service and the affidavit, the lien cannot be enforced.

serve_on: owner or person believed to be owner
parameters.required_document: proof of service affidavit signed by person serving

rules.citation: AB 457 (2010); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien content and service provision
rules.verbatim_quote: Notice of Mechanics Lien be served on the owner or person believed to be the owner of the property or on the construction lender or original contractor, and that a “proof of service affidavit” ... be completed and signed by the person serving the Notice of Mechanics Lien. ... will cause the mechanics lien to be unenforceable.
rules.notes: Under the current Civil Code, service on the lender or original contractor is generally an alternative only when the owner cannot be served. The proof of service is attached to the lien when recorded (extractor's note; verify).

rules.title: Bonded stop notice to lender: bond = 1.25 x claim
rules.plain_english: To bind a construction lender, a stop notice must be accompanied by a bond equal to 1.25 times the claim, delivered in person or by certified or registered mail to whoever administers or holds the construction funds. If the claimant loses, it must pay the costs awarded to the owner, contractor or lender.

parameters.deliver_to: persons responsible for administering or holding construction funds
parameters.claimant_liability_if_loses: all costs awarded to owner, contractor, or construction lender

rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants serving construction lenders (private works)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code bonded stop payment notice provision
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 78 and 81
rules.verbatim_quote: To bind a construction lender, the stop notice must be bonded. The bond that accompanies a stop notice to any construction lender must be in the sum equal to 1 ¼ times the amount of the claim. The bond must be delivered along with the stop notice in person or by certified or registered mail to the responsible parties for administering or holding the construction funds.
rules.notes: Also stated in the glossary entry 'Bonded Stop Notice' on page 78. Exceptions under current law (for example, a direct contractor's notice to a lender) are not stated here.

rules.title: Claim of Lien: required contents (signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Claim of Lien must be signed and verified by the claimant or its agent and state the five items listed in the parameters, including the demand after credits and offsets and a site description sufficient for identification.

required_fields: amount of claimant's demand after deducting credits and offsets
name of owner or reputed owner, if known
kind of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished
name of person who employed claimant or to whom claimant furnished labor/services/equipment/materials
description of the site sufficient for identification

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien content provision
rules.verbatim_quote: Claim of Lien (mechanics lien) is a written statement signed and verified by the claimant or by the claimant’s agent that must state the following: 1. The amount of claimant’s demand (after deducting credits and offsets). 2. The name of the owner or reputed owner, if known. 3. The kind of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished by the claimant.
rules.notes: Items 4 and 5 are in the parameters. Current law also requires the claimant's address, a Notice of Mechanics Lien statement and proof of service (see notice-of-mechanics-lien-service-and-proof); verify the full list before generating forms.

rules.title: Notice of Cessation: required contents (owner signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Notice of Cessation is signed and verified by the owner or agent and states the six items listed in the parameters, from the approximate date labor stopped to the original contractor's name.

required_fields: approximate date labor stopped
confirmation that no further labor has been performed since recording
name and address of owner
nature of owner's interest or estate
street address of site or description sufficient for identification
name of original contractor, if any

rules.applies_to: Project owners recording a Notice of Cessation
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of cessation provision
rules.verbatim_quote: Notice of Cessation is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Approximate date when labor on the job stopped. 2. Confirmation that no further labor has been performed since the recording of the notice. 3. Name and address of the owner. 4. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner.
rules.notes: Items 5 and 6 are in the parameters.

rules.title: Notice of Completion: required contents (owner signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Notice of Completion is signed and verified by the owner or agent and states the five items listed in the parameters, from the completion date to the original contractor for the completed work.

required_fields: date the job was finished
name and address of owner
nature of owner's interest or estate
street address of site or description sufficient for identification
name of original contractor, if any, for the contract covering the completed portion

rules.applies_to: Project owners recording a Notice of Completion
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision
rules.verbatim_quote: Notice of Completion is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Date that the job was finished. 2. Name and address of the owner. 3. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner. 4. Street address of the site, if any, or a description of the site sufficient for identification.
rules.notes: Item 5 is in the parameters.

parameters.record_with: county recorder of county where site is located
parameters.if_not_timely: claimants get the 90-day lien recording period

rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision

rules.title: Lien recording deadline: 60 days (prime) / 30 days (sub) after NOC; else 90 days
rules.plain_english: If a valid Notice of Completion is recorded, a prime contractor has 60 days and a subcontractor 30 days to record a mechanics lien. If no timely notice is recorded, the deadline is 90 days.
rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines
rules.verbatim_quote: If the Notice of Completion is recorded, then the time within which you must record your mechanics lien is 60 days if you are a prime contractor and 30 days if you are a subcontractor. If this notice is not filed in a timely manner, you have a 90-day period within which to record the claim.
rules.notes: This is the core lien deadline lookup. A Notice of Cessation shortens deadlines the same way (pages 75-77). The 90-day period runs from completion, which pages 76-77 describe as cessation plus use, or acceptance.

rules.title: Notice of Non-Responsibility: required contents
rules.plain_english: An owner or interest-holder who did not order the work (for example, a landlord whose tenant hired the contractor) can give a signed and verified Notice of Non-Responsibility. It must contain the four items listed in the parameters, ending with a statement that they will NOT be responsible for claims.

parameters.signed_and_verified_by: person owning/claiming interest who did not cause the work, or that person's agent
required_fields: description of site sufficient for identification
name and nature of title or interest of person giving notice
name of purchaser or lessee, if known
statement that person will NOT be responsible for claims arising from the work
parameters.typical_use: landlord whose tenant ordered the work

rules.applies_to: Property owners/landlords whose tenants or purchasers order work; contractors working for tenants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of non-responsibility provision
rules.verbatim_quote: This notice must contain: 1. Description of the site sufficient for identification. 2. Name and nature of the title or interest of the person giving the notice. 3. Name of the purchaser or person holding the lease (lessee), if known. 4. Statement by the person giving the notice that they will ... NOT be responsible for any claims arising from the work of improvement.
rules.notes: Contractors working for a tenant should check for a recorded notice. It can defeat a lien against the owner's interest.

rules.title: Notice of Non-Responsibility: post on site and record within 10 days of discovery
rules.plain_english: Within 10 days of discovering the work, the person asserting non-responsibility must post the notice in a conspicuous place on the site and record it with the county recorder.

parameters.trigger: discovery of the work of improvement
actions: post in conspicuous place on site
record with county recorder of county where site is located

rules.applies_to: Property owners/interest holders who did not cause the work
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of non-responsibility provision
rules.verbatim_quote: Within 10 days of discovering the work of improvement, the person asserting non-responsibility must post this notice in a conspicuous place on the site and must record the notice in the Office of the County Recorder of the county in which the site is located.
rules.notes: Both posting and recording are required.
