rules.title: Definitions: original (prime) contractor; owner
rules.plain_english: The original or prime contractor (usually a general contractor) contracts directly with the owner. 'Owner' includes anyone with title or an interest in the real property.

parameters.owner_scope: any person having some title or interest in the parcel

rules.verbatim_quote: Original Contractor, also known as prime contractor, is usually a general contractor. Owner includes any person(s) having some title or interest in a parcel of real property.
rules.notes: Current Civil Code term: 'direct contractor'.

rules.title: Definition: subcontractor (no direct contract with owner)
rules.plain_english: A subcontractor is anyone without a direct contract with the owner who contracts with the prime contractor or another subcontractor. Subs are usually specialty contractors but can be general contractors. This role decides which lien deadlines apply.
rules.verbatim_quote: Subcontractor is any person who does not have a contract directly with an owner. The subcontractor has a contract with and from the prime contractor or another subcontractor. A subcontractor is usually a specialty contractor but can also be a general contractor.

rules.title: Definitions: lien foreclosure action; lis pendens
rules.plain_english: A lien foreclosure action is the lawsuit to enforce a mechanics lien. A lis pendens is a recorded notice that a pending lawsuit affects the real property, warning buyers they may be bound by the judgment.
rules.verbatim_quote: Lien Foreclosure Action is a lawsuit to foreclose the mechanics lien. Lis Pendens is a notice that a lawsuit is pending, and that the lawsuit affects real property. It warns everyone who might acquire the property that they may be bound by an adverse judgment.

rules.title: Payment bond substitutes for the property as lien security
rules.plain_english: A payment bond, usually bought by the owner or contractor, is large enough to pay all claimants. Claimants can sue on the bond, which replaces the real property as security against mechanics liens.

parameters.amount: sufficient to pay all claims of claimants
parameters.effect: substitutes bond for real property as security

rules.verbatim_quote: Payment Bond is a bond usually procured by the owner or contractor in an amount sufficient to pay all claims of claimants. The bond gives the claimant the right to recover in any suit brought on the bond. Usually, the bond is used to protect against mechanics liens and substitutes the bond as security instead of the real property.
rules.notes: Statutory bond amount percentages (for example for public works) are not stated here.

rules.title: Stop Notice: required contents (signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A stop notice is a signed and verified notice telling a lender or other fund holder that money is owed. It must state the three items listed in the parameters, including the value of work already furnished and of the whole job.

required_fields: type of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished
name of person to or for whom furnished
amount (value as near as possible) of work/equipment already completed or furnished, and amount of whole work agreed

rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants (private and public works)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice provisions
rules.verbatim_quote: Stop Notice is a written notice, signed and verified by the claimant or the claimant’s agent, that puts a lender or anyone else holding construction funds on notice that there is money due and owed to the claimant. It must state the following: 1. Type of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished by the claimant.
rules.notes: Items 2 and 3 are in the parameters. Current term: 'stop payment notice'.

rules.title: Stop notice service on private works: owner/architect; lender branch manager
rules.plain_english: On private works, deliver the stop notice to the owner personally, leave it with a person in charge at their residence or business, or deliver it to their architect. For a lender with branches, deliver to the manager or responsible person at the branch holding the construction funds.

rules.title: Stop notice on public works: file with state department director or public disbursing officer
rules.plain_english: On state public works, file the stop notice with the director of the department that started the contract. On other public works, file it with the controller, auditor or other disbursing officer who pays under the contract, or with the body that awarded the contract.

parameters.state_public_work_file_with: director of the department that initiated the contract

rules.title: Stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail
rules.plain_english: Any stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail, which has the same effect as personal service.
rules.verbatim_quote: Any stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail with the same effect as personal service.

rules.title: Fund holder must withhold enough to cover the stop notice or be liable
rules.plain_english: A lender, owner or other party holding construction funds that receives a stop notice must withhold enough money to cover it. If it doesn't, it may be directly liable to the claimant.

parameters.obligation: withhold funds sufficient to satisfy stop notice amount
parameters.consequence_of_failure: fund holder may be directly liable to claimant

If the person holding the funds does not withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the stop notice, then the lender or whoever else is holding the funds may be responsible to the claimant directly.

rules.title: Government bids may require steps toward minority, women and DVBE goals
rules.plain_english: Federal, state and local agencies, utilities and some private corporations may require bidders to take specific steps toward minority, women and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) participation goals. For state contracts, check with the DGS Office of Small Business and DVBE Services.

rules.notes: Goal percentages and good-faith-effort steps are not stated here; they are set by each agency.

rules.title: Call 811 at least 2 working days, no more than 14 calendar days, before excavating
rules.plain_english: Anyone planning to excavate must contact the regional notification center (call 811, free) at least two working days, and no more than 14 calendar days, before starting. The center issues an inquiry (ticket) number confirming the call. Emergencies are excluded.

rules.title: Mark excavation boundaries (usually white paint) before operators mark
rules.plain_english: Before excavating, clearly mark the boundaries of the work area at the site, usually with white paint.
rules.verbatim_quote: At the site, excavators must clearly mark the boundaries of the work area, usually with white paint.

rules.title: Operators mark lines in color code or advise clearance
rules.plain_english: After notification, utility operators must give information about their facilities within your marked area and mark or stake their lines in the correct color, or tell you the area is clear. Operators answer only for facilities they own.

operator_actions: mark or stake lines using appropriate color code

rules.applies_to: Subsurface installation operators; excavators waiting for marks
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 84 and 86
rules.verbatim_quote: Within these boundary markings, operators of underground installations must then provide information about their facilities, mark or stake the location of their lines clearly using the appropriate color to show what type of installation is present or advise of clearance.
rules.notes: Page 84: operators are only responsible for facilities they own.

rules.title: Request re-marking when marks are no longer visible
rules.plain_english: If utility markings become unreadable during the job, contact the notification center and ask that the operator re-mark the lines within two working days.

parameters.action: contact regional center to request re-mark

rules.verbatim_quote: During the course of the job, if the operator’s markings become no longer visible, the excavator must contact the regional center and request that the operator re-mark the lines within two working days.
rules.notes: The wording is ambiguous: 'within two working days' most naturally reads as the operator's re-mark window, not a deadline for the excavator's request.

rules.title: Pothole with hand tools or vacuum before using power equipment
rules.plain_english: Using the operator's marks, find the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before using any power equipment.
rules.verbatim_quote: Using the operator’s markings, an excavator must determine the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before any power equipment may be used.
rules.notes: The tolerance zone width is not stated in this source.

rules.title: New subsurface installations after Jan 1, 2023 must be GIS-mapped
rules.plain_english: All new underground installations after January 1, 2023 must be mapped in a geographic information system and kept as permanent records by the operator.
rules.applies_to: Operators of subsurface installations (and contractors installing for them)
rules.verbatim_quote: After January 1, 2023, all new subsurface installations must be mapped using a geographic information system and maintained as permanent records of the operator.
rules.notes: This obligation falls on the operator. Contractors installing utilities may be asked to supply as-built GIS data.

rules.title: Report damage to the notification center within 48 hours
rules.plain_english: If you discover or cause damage to an underground facility, notify the regional notification center within 48 hours.

parameters.trigger: discovering or causing damage to subsurface installation

rules.verbatim_quote: An excavator must notify the regional notification center within 48 hours of discovering or causing damage.
rules.notes: Separate immediate-notification duties (operator, 911 for gas or hazardous liquid releases) may also apply but are not stated here.

rules.title: Information to give when calling 811
rules.plain_english: When requesting a ticket, give the start date and time, your name and company details, the nature of the work, who it is for, the foreman, the permit name and number, whether the area is white-lined, and a detailed site location.

ticket_fields: whether excavation outlined in white paint
site description: address, side of street, intersection corner, footage and total distances or tie-in measurements, nearest intersecting street, city, county

rules.verbatim_quote: Give your name, company’s name, company’s mailing address, email address, telephone number where you can be contacted, nature of work (grading, drilling, etc.), whom the work is being done for, name of the foreman, permit name and number, if excavation has been outlined in white paint, and a description of the excavation site.
rules.notes: Good template for a pre-filled 811 request form.

rules.title: USA negligent violation: fine up to $10,000
rules.plain_english: An operator or excavator who negligently violates the 811 law can be fined up to $10,000.
rules.verbatim_quote: Any operator or excavator who negligently violates any portion of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 is subject to a fine not to exceed $10,000.
rules.notes: The penalty provision is believed to be Gov. Code 4216.6 (extractor's note).

rules.plain_english: An operator or excavator who knowingly and willfully violates the 811 law can be fined up to $50,000.

rules.plain_english: If a knowing and willful violation damages a gas or hazardous liquid pipeline and flammable, toxic or corrosive gas or liquid escapes, the civil penalty can reach $100,000.

escape of flammable, toxic, or corrosive gas or liquid

rules.title: USA violations: third-party damage claims and CSLB discipline
rules.plain_english: Beyond fines, excavators can face third-party damage claims. A willful or deliberate violation of the 811 law is grounds for CSLB discipline, which can include license revocation (B&P 7110(f)).

parameters.civil_exposure: third party claims for damages from excavation work (CSLB narrative; no statute in book)
parameters.license_discipline_mental_state: willful or deliberate disregard and violation of Gov. Code 4216 et seq.

rules.title: Which 811 center serves each California county
rules.plain_english: Both centers are reached by dialing 811. USA North (usanorth811.org) serves 49 Northern and Central California counties plus Nevada. DigAlert (digalert.org) serves 9 Southern California counties.
rules.verbatim_quote: Underground Service Alert of Southern California: 811 www.digalert.org Serves the following counties in Southern California: Imperial, Inyo, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara, and Ventura
rules.notes: 49 + 9 = 58 counties, all of California.

rules.title: Human remains found: stop all work nearby and call the county coroner
rules.plain_english: If human remains or burial artifacts are found anywhere other than a dedicated cemetery, immediately stop all excavation at the site and any nearby area that may contain remains, and contact the county coroner.

parameters.trigger: discovery or recognition of human remains or burial artifacts outside a dedicated cemetery
actions: stop all work at site and nearby area reasonably suspected to contain remains

rules.applies_to: Contractors, excavators and property owners on any site
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 7050.5; Pub. Resources Code 5097.9-5097.991
rules.verbatim_quote: In the event of discovery or recognition of any human remains in any location other than a dedicated cemetery, there shall be no further excavation or disturbance of the site or nearby area. ... Stop all work immediately at that site and any nearby area reasonably suspected to have remains and contact the county coroner.

rules.title: Coroner: 2 working days to examine; 24 hours to notify NAHC if Native American
rules.plain_english: The coroner has two working days after notification to examine the remains. If they are Native American, the coroner has 24 hours to notify the Native American Heritage Commission. Work stays stopped meanwhile.

parameters.clock_start: coroner notified by person responsible for excavation

rules.applies_to: Projects with discovered human remains (owners and contractors track the work stoppage)
rules.verbatim_quote: The coroner has two working days to examine the remains after being notified by the person responsible for the excavation. If the remains are Native American, the coroner has 24 hours to notify the Native American Heritage Commission.
rules.notes: These are agency deadlines, useful for estimating the minimum work-stoppage duration.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.88. Health & Safety Code 7050.5 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: NAHC notifies most likely descendant; MLD has 24 hours to recommend treatment
rules.plain_english: The NAHC immediately notifies the most likely descendant (MLD), who then has 24 hours to recommend to the owner how to treat and dispose of the remains and grave goods with dignity.
rules.applies_to: Property owners and contractors on sites with Native American remains
rules.verbatim_quote: The Native American Heritage Commission will immediately notify the person it believes to be the most likely descendant of the deceased Native American. 4. The most likely descendant has 24 hours to make recommendations to the owner or representative for the treatment and disposition, with proper dignity, of the remains and grave goods.
rules.notes: The book says 24 hours. The extractor believes current PRC 5097.98(a) gives descendants 48 hours after being granted site access; verify before hard-coding. The citation section is inferred, since the book cites the range 5097.9-5097.991.

The book's 24-hour figure may be out of date. Do not hard-code 24 hours.

rules.title: Owner may request NAHC mediation; if it fails, reinter on-site
rules.plain_english: If the owner does not accept the descendant's recommendations, either side may ask the NAHC to mediate. If mediation fails, the landowner must reinter the remains and associated items with dignity, in a spot on the property that will not be disturbed again.

parameters.step_1: owner rejects MLD recommendations -> owner or MLD may request NAHC mediation
parameters.step_2: mediation fails -> landowner reinters remains and burial items with dignity on property
parameters.reinterment_location_requirement: not subject to further subsurface disturbance

rules.verbatim_quote: If the owner doesn’t accept the descendant’s recommendations, the owner or the descendant may request mediation by the Native American Heritage Commission. ... the landowner or their authorized representative shall reinter the human remains and items associated with Native American burials, with appropriate dignity, and in a location on the property not subject to further subsurface disturbance.
rules.notes: This affects site planning: the reinterment area becomes a permanent no-dig zone. Section number inferred from the book's range citation.

rules.title: Removing or possessing Native American remains or grave goods is a felony
rules.plain_english: Knowingly or willfully removing, taking or keeping Native American remains or burial artifacts without legal authority is a felony punishable by state prison.
rules.applies_to: Anyone, including contractors and workers on excavation sites
rules.verbatim_quote: Any person who knowingly or willfully removes, obtains, or possesses any Native American remains or associated burial artifacts, without authority of law, is guilty of a felony, punishable by imprisonment in state prison.
rules.notes: NAHC contact: (916) 373-3710, nahc@nahc.ca.gov, www.nahc.ca.gov.

verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.89. PRC 5097.94, 5097.98 and 5097.99 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: C-57 Water Well license required to drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy wells
rules.plain_english: Only a person holding a C-57 Water Well Contractor license may dig, bore, drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well or geothermal heat exchange well.
rules.applies_to: Anyone performing well construction, alteration, abandonment or destruction
rules.verbatim_quote: No person shall undertake to dig, bore, or drill a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well, to deepen or reperforate such a well, or to abandon or destroy such a well, unless the person responsible for that construction, alteration, destruction, or abandonment possesses a C-57 Water Well Contractor’s License.
rules.notes: Useful as a license-class check: job type 'well' requires C-57.

rules.title: File Well Completion Report (DWR 188) within 60 days
rules.plain_english: Anyone who builds, alters (drills, deepens, reperforates, abandons) or destroys a water, cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal heat exchange well must file a Well Completion Report (DWR 188) with DWR within 60 days after finishing. This also applies when converting an oil or gas well to one of those uses.

parameters.form: Well Completion Report, DWR 188 (formerly Water Well Driller's Report; a.k.a. well log/driller's log)
activities: convert oil or gas well to water/cathodic/monitoring well
parameters.filing_system: Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR)

rules.applies_to: C-57 contractors and others constructing, altering, destroying or converting wells
rules.verbatim_quote: people who construct, alter (including, but not limited to, drilling, deepening, reperforation, or abandonment), or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well, to file a report of completion, called the “Well Completion Report, DWR 188,” with the California Department of Water Resources (DWR) within 60 days after completion of the work.
rules.notes: The quoted sentence begins 'California Water Code sections 13751 through 13754 require...'. File through OSWCR with an account tied to the C-57 license (page 91).

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.90 (OSWCR filing details match p.91)
verification.correction: Quote matches PDF p.90 (OSWCR filing details match p.91). Water Code 13751-13754 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 60-day deadline cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Failure to file Well Completion Report: misdemeanor and license discipline
rules.plain_english: Not filing the Well Completion Report is a misdemeanor (Water Code 13754, per the book). A willful or deliberate violation of the water-well provisions is also grounds for CSLB discipline against your license (B&P 7110(e)).

parameters.violation: failure to file Well Completion Report
parameters.offense_level: misdemeanor (Water Code 13754 per book summary; primary text not in book)
parameters.license_consequence: cause for disciplinary action when the violation is a willful or deliberate disregard and violation of H&S Code or Water Code provisions relating to digging, boring or drilling water wells (B&P 7110(e))

rules.citation: Water Code 13754 (misdemeanor, per book); B&P 7110(e) (license discipline)
rules.source_location: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 90 (summary); PDF page 351 (B&P 7110)
rules.verbatim_quote: NOTE: Failure to file the Well Completion Report is a misdemeanor (Water Code §13754) and constitutes cause for disciplinary action against your contractor license (Business and Professions Code section 7110). | B&P 7110: "Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of ... (e) Any provision of the Health and Safety Code or Water Code, relating to the digging, boring, or drilling of water wells ... constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee."

verification.checked_against: 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt): PDF p.90 (summary); PDF p.351 B&P 7110(e)
verification.correction: License-discipline part: B&P 7110(e) makes a "willful or deliberate disregard and violation" of Health & Safety Code or Water Code provisions on digging, boring or drilling water wells a cause for discipline. The book's note that failure to file "constitutes cause for disciplinary action" leaves out that condition. Added the condition and the subdivision cite. 7110(e) names water wells only; whether it reaches cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal wells is not stated. The misdemeanor classification (Water Code 13754) is not in the book and remains unverifiable.

rules.title: File well reports online via OSWCR with a C-57-based account
rules.plain_english: Drillers file Well Completion Reports through DWR's Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR), using an account tied to their C-57 license that DWR validates.

parameters.system: Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR)

rules.verbatim_quote: Drillers submit their well completion reports to DWR with the Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR). OSWCR users create an account based on their C-57 license that DWR will validate. Upon approval, users will be able to submit Well Completion Reports.
rules.notes: Set up the OSWCR account before the first job so DWR validation does not eat into the 60-day filing window.

rules.title: Follow DWR Bulletin 74 well standards and local well ordinances and permits
rules.plain_english: Well construction, modification, rehabilitation and destruction must follow DWR Bulletin 74 (California Well Standards, Bulletins 74-81 and 74-90) plus any stricter local ordinances. Contact the local enforcing agency (usually county environmental health) before any well work; many require a permit and fee.

state_standards: DWR Bulletin 74-90 California Well Standards (draft supplement)

rules.applies_to: Well contractors (C-57) and owners planning well work
rules.citation: None cited (DWR Bulletin 74; local well ordinances)
rules.verbatim_quote: The designated local enforcing agency, which is usually the county environmental health department, should be contacted whenever work on a well is being planned to ensure compliance with local ordinances. Many of these local agencies require permits for any work on a well and charge a fee for that permit.
rules.notes: Permit fees vary by county and are not stated.
